_comment: Demo dataset for `occ pipelinq:demo:seed` (DemoSeedService). Every object is marked with the '[Demo]' prefix on its lookup field (client.name / contact.name / pipeline.title / product.name / lead.title / ticket.title / task.subject / appointmentService.name / appointmentResource.name / appointmentBooking.subject / journey.name / socialAccount.displayName / socialPost.title; search rows carry the demo property and source instead, and a keyword target a '[Demo]' note) so the seed is idempotent (exact-match lookup) and removable (--remove deletes exactly this set). Date placeholders: '@days:N' -> Y-m-d today+N, '@datetime:N' -> ISO-8601 today+N, '@week:D' -> Y-m-d of day D (0 = Monday) this week, '@week:DTHH:MM' -> ISO-8601 that day at that time. openspec/changes/align-claims-and-first-hour REQ-SETUP-PIP-008.
_coverageNote: The contacts / pipelines / products / complaints / tasks sections were added 2026-08-06. Measured on run 31082256226: the CONTACTS, TASKS and PIPELINES index pages had a genuinely empty collection on a fresh install — the base register ships example objects for products (14), clients, leads, tickets and the POS entities, but none at all for contact, task or pipeline — so CnIndexPage rendered `cn-index-page__empty` and no data table, silently, with no console error and no failed request. Every 'the list table renders' assertion in tests/e2e/spec-coverage failed for a reason that pointed at the page rather than at the fixture. Products was NOT empty; the extra rows here exist so the seeded set is coherent (a client has contact persons) rather than to repair that page.

_appointmentsNote: The appointment sections back the Services and resources page (openspec/changes/services-and-resources-at-a-glance task 4.1): seven services (five bookable online, one draft that no resource matches), the desks and desk staff they match, and bookings in the current week. They live here, not in the example register, because '@week:D' resolves to day D (0 = Monday) of the week the seed runs as a date, and '@week:DTHH:MM' to that day at that time; each booking links its customer (customerKey), its service (serviceKey) and the resource of each assignment (resourceKey) to the objects saved earlier in the run.

_journeysNote: Journeys are saved through JourneyService so each compiles into a flow, and are held to draft or paused so that flow is never enabled. Each journey's `runs` fill the run log on its detail page; a run names a demo contact (contactKey) and client (clientKey), and its `reason` is one of the codes the run log puts into words.

_socialNote: Fills the Social performance ranking. The accounts are inactive and hold no credential, so the daily follower refresh leaves their followerCount alone and the composer never offers them; the publications carry no externalId, so the daily metrics pull keeps their numbers and calls no network. Views stay 0: Mastodon and LinkedIn do not report them, and the metrics service never borrows a number. One publication has no metrics yet, which the ranking sorts last.

_searchNote: Fills the Keyword intelligence page. The rows stand in for a Search Console import: each query/page is split over two days inside the page's default 28-day window, and they are shaped to land in every derivation — all four position buckets, three striking-distance queries (positions 8-20 with a click rate under the expected curve), one cannibalisation (two pages sharing a query, the combined rate well below the better page's) and one query under the 100-impression floor. The query text has to read as real search, so the rows are marked by `property` and `source` rather than a [Demo] prefix, and removal deletes exactly the rows carrying both. The content gap check needs a crawl source, so it keeps saying none is configured.
